title: David Roberts Welsh Journal
sourceTitle: FAMILY HISTORY, WRITINGS AND POEMS of DAVID ROBERTS, NATIVE OF LLANFROTHEN, MEIRIONETHSHIRE, WALES
primaryWriter: David Roberts and later Roberts family contributors
language: Primarily Welsh, with later English additions and inserted printed material
description: One physically two-ended family volume containing Welsh poetry and other writings, a Welsh family-history and journal sequence, later family additions, and inserted printed material.
sourceIdentityNote: This is one physical source begun by David Roberts and later continued, copied, translated, annotated, or supplemented by Roberts family contributors. The site does not attribute the entire volume to one hand.
physicalStructureNote: Verified PDF structure: covers on pages 1 and 110; poetry/writings on pages 2-62; inserted/printed poetry on pages 63-66; family-history title leaf on page 67; family-history/journal sequence on pages 68-109.
exportStatus: Welsh transcription, modern English translation, bilingual Word, and combined PDF exports are defined for later generation from these same page Markdown files; they are not published as complete while nearly all pages remain untranscribed.

attributionModel.historicalConstraint: David Roberts died November 4, 1858; post-death material is not attributed as newly written by him.

pages.editor: D. R. Roberts (as written; identity unresolved)

pages.sourceTranscriptionLabel: Source transcription (English title label and Welsh handwriting)
pages.contentContext: Family-history title leaf. The pasted label identifies David Roberts and the Llanfrothen/Festiniog context; Welsh writing above the label is preserved separately from the English label.

pages.pageLanguage: Primarily Welsh; later additions may include English
pages.attributionBasis: The page is dated January 6, 1854, names David Roberts beside the heading Fy Hanes, and uses first-person family and marriage statements. These features support David Roberts as probable content author and scribe, but no separate signature or independently attributable handwriting sample confirms the physical hand.

relatedJournalPassages.basis: The Welsh and RDR passages share the January 6, 1854 heading, first-person ancestry structure, names, marriages, residences, children, and sequence.

pages.contentContext: Opening first-person Welsh ancestry and family-history entry dated January 6, 1854; it continues onto PDF page 69 and has a confirmed historical-English parallel on RDR PDF page 3.

pages.pageLanguage: Primarily Welsh; later additions may include English
pages.attributionBasis: The first-person family narrative continues directly from the dated Fy Hanes entry on page 68 in the same compact Welsh hand and ink. This supports David Roberts as probable content author and scribe, but damage and the absence of a separate signature or independently attributable handwriting sample prevent confirmation.

relatedJournalPassages.basis: The Welsh continuation and RDR page 3 share the Daniel and Gwen family notice and the transition into John Roberts's family.

The Welsh and RDR passages share the John, Edward, Robert, and Elinor family sequence, Vermont setting, child list, burial context, and four-line verse position; RDR preserves fuller prose than the damaged Welsh manuscript.

pages.contentContext: Continuation of the January 6, 1854 Welsh family-history entry, including Roberts-family notices, extensive erased and abraded text, and a damaged four-line verse; it continues toward PDF page 70.

pages.pageLanguage: Primarily Welsh; later additions may include English
pages.attributionBasis: The page explicitly shifts into first-person personal history and continues the same compact Welsh hand and ink used in the dated Fy Hanes entry on pages 68-69. This supports David Roberts as probable content author and scribe, but no signature or independently attributable handwriting sample confirms the physical hand.

relatedJournalPassages.basis: The Welsh and RDR passages share the closing family notice, explicit transition to personal narrative, and opening account of poverty and childhood labor.
The Welsh and RDR passages share the childhood occupations, illness, Festiniog quarry work, Cae and Cwmstradlyn episode, schooling, religious inclination, and poetic ambition in the same sequence.

pages.contentContext: Continuation of the January 6, 1854 family history, followed by an explicit transition into David Roberts's first-person autobiography; the final sentence continues onto PDF page 71.
